warnings: no_prevalence: counts of sources are not counts of buyers; no job carries an observed market frequency

language_samples_are_source_language: quoted fragments are language from the cited source, including one secondary characterisation of forum discussion (source-007), not a measured distribution of how travellers phrase things

roles_defined: role-001 first-time travel-data buyer; role-002 experienced multi-country traveller; role-003 heavy-data remote worker; role-004 traveller in destination with a failing or expiring line

jobs.statement: When a trip to one foreign country is booked, help a traveller arrive with working mobile data instead of paying home-carrier roaming, while their handset must support a digital line and stay unlocked.
jobs.struggling_moment: Departure is near and the only default is per-day home-carrier roaming.
jobs.desired_progress: Phone data that works on landing, at a known total cost, bought before the flight.
workarounds: Buying a physical local SIM after landing
Relying on hotel and cafe WiFi

push: Not wanting to hunt for a shop after landing
anxiety: Will it actually activate when I land
habit: Just turning on the carrier roaming pass

language_samples.text: which eSIM should I get for Japan?
Best eSIM for Bali in 2026? Coverage & speed experiences

jobs.statement: When an itinerary crosses several countries, help a traveller keep one working data plan across borders instead of buying and reinstalling a plan per country.
jobs.struggling_moment: Data stops or has to be re-bought every time the traveller crosses into the next country.
jobs.desired_progress: One plan whose coverage list matches the whole itinerary.
workarounds: A separate local plan per country

pull: Regional and global packages with published country lists
anxiety: Is my exact country list actually covered
Does the plan restart or carry over
habit: Buying per-country at each arrival airport

criteria: Validity window covers the whole trip

language_samples.text: List of Prepaid SIM threads (country-specific and multi-country)

jobs.statement: When a traveller cannot tell how much data a trip needs or whether an unlimited plan is genuinely unlimited, help them size the plan and avoid fair-use throttling while tethering a laptop.
jobs.struggling_moment: Plans are sold in gigabytes or as 'unlimited' with an undisclosed daily threshold.
jobs.desired_progress: A defensible data volume choice and a clear expectation of what happens after the threshold.
workarounds: Rationing usage and staying on WiFi

anxiety: Paying for data that expires unused

constraints: Fair-use throttling near 1 Mbps after roughly 3 GB/day on unlimited regional plans

language_samples.text: How Much Data Do You Need for Europe Travel?
Speed is capped at approximately 1 Mbps once you exceed the daily fair-use threshold

jobs.statement: When a traveller is unsure whether their handset can take a foreign data line at all, help them verify eSIM support, carrier lock and device origin before they pay for anything.
jobs.struggling_moment: The purchase may be wasted if the handset is locked or has no eSIM support.
jobs.desired_progress: A yes/no answer about this specific handset, and the unlock step if the answer is no.
workarounds: Asking the home carrier to unlock
Borrowing or buying a second handset

push: Risk of a non-refundable useless purchase
pull: A quick device check before buying
anxiety: Handset bought in a region without eSIM support

constraints: Handsets from China, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan may lack support

language_samples.text: How do I check if my iOS device supports eSIM?

jobs.statement: When a traveller relies on their home number for messaging apps and bank verification codes, help them keep those working while a separate data-only line carries the internet.
jobs.struggling_moment: A data-only travel line has no voice or SMS and often no local number.
jobs.desired_progress: Confidence that the home number, messaging apps and one-time codes keep working, plus the dual-line setup steps.
workarounds: Leaving home roaming on as well

push: Fear of losing bank one-time codes abroad
pull: Dual-line handsets keep the home number active
anxiety: Accidental roaming charges from the home line
habit: Swapping physical SIMs and losing the home number

language_samples.text: Can I Use WhatsApp with an eSIM?
Local phone number not always included

jobs.statement: When a traveller lands and the phone shows no service despite a plan bought before the flight, help them restore connectivity from the airport without another handset.
jobs.struggling_moment: The line is installed but not carrying data, and the traveller is offline in an unfamiliar country.
jobs.desired_progress: Working data in minutes, or a clear escalation path.

anxiety: Line cannot be moved to another handset

constraints: Traveller may have no data to reach support
Line is bound to the handset

language_samples.text: Why is my eSIM not working?
you cannot pull the eSIM and slot it into a friend's phone

jobs.statement: When a plan is running out or about to expire mid-trip, help a traveller extend the existing line rather than lose it and start again.
jobs.struggling_moment: Data or validity is about to end while the traveller is still abroad.
jobs.desired_progress: Continued service at a known incremental cost, without reinstalling.

pull: Top-up in the app without a new line
anxiety: Whether unused data or validity carries over

criteria: Whether the same line is retained

language_samples.text: When does my eSIM data package expire?
top up your eSIM - you don't need to buy a new eSIM to stay connected

jobs.statement: When public reporting says travellers are shifting away from operator roaming, help a traveller understand what has actually changed about buying data abroad this year.
jobs.struggling_moment: The traveller has heard the default is changing but cannot tell what is marketing and what is real.
jobs.desired_progress: A dated, sourced picture of how travel connectivity is bought now.

pull: Reported shift toward third-party travel data

constraints: Story evidence decays and must carry a review-by date

language_samples.text: travel eSIM adoption is now a primary driver of retail roaming spend

jobs.statement: When a destination may require identity registration for a mobile line, help a traveller find out whether that applies to a digital line bought before departure.
jobs.struggling_moment: The traveller cannot tell whether a pre-bought digital line escapes local registration rules.
jobs.desired_progress: A destination-specific answer and the documents needed if registration applies.
workarounds: Registering a local SIM in person on arrival

push: Risk of a line that will not activate

constraints: Retrieved evidence names no specific countries and is undated

language_samples.text: Do not assume that eSIM automatically means no verification
